text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein says: "The alternative to peace is much uglier than what we imagine, what worries me is that the minority is capable of terrorising the majority in the region."
- State sector doctors decide on work stoggage from October 26 over pay dispute.
- Cabinet is briefed by Prime Minister Kabariti on king's talks in Washington with U.S. officials on Middle East peace and bilateral ties and assistance to kingdom.
- Crown Prince says "without stability no economic projects can be implemented and no alternative to the peace process and abandoning it is a catastrophe for all of us."
- Israeli Prime Minster Netanyahu says political differences between Israel and Jordan are a "natural matter" and sends his envoy to Jordan.
- A letter from the interior minister to the prime minister to boost the financial situation of local governorates.

- King says "all progress in peace process and treaties in jeopardy if Israel does not fulfil commitments, agreements are sacred and cannot be tampered with...Netanyahu has to deal with Palestinian leader Arafat as an equal partner."
- U.S. mediator briefs Kabariti on progress of Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.
- King invites Dubia leader to visit.
- Government leaning towards reducing income tax and expanding sales tax on consumption.
